key_insight: Training the departure-time forecaster end-to-end with the EV charging policy improves control decisions more than optimizing forecast accuracy alone.
engineering_relevance: For smart charging systems, using decision-focused learning can reduce wasted charging and help manage grid load more effectively under missing or uncertain user information.
method: Use RL to learn a charging policy from historical EV charging patterns.
Estimate unknown departure times with a forecaster, but train it jointly with the controller.
Backpropagate policy feedback into the forecaster so predictions are optimized for decision quality, not just accuracy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation against baselines with up to 14% higher total reward and 55% less unsupplied energy than RL without departure-time forecasting.
watch_item: Joint training may be harder to stabilize and may require careful integration, since forecast errors and policy updates can interact nonlinearly.
paper_title: Forecasting what Matters: Decision-Focused RL for Controlled EV Charging with Unknown Departure Times
